youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Farzin Irani around concerns a New Zealand–India trade deal could accelerate digital payment systems and central bank digital currencies. They discuss growing economic pressure at home, with rising living costs, a weakening housing market, and warnings of stagflation. They also discuss fuel supply risks and preparing for coming economic turmoil as shortages begin to hit every aspect of the global economy. Farzin has updated his website with new free resources to help people prepare for the future. Discover more from Farzin on Linktr.ee DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation.

youtube.title: FREDDIE PONTON
youtube.summary: Freddie Ponton joins Paul Brennan for an update on the situation in Gaza, since the Iran War pushed it out of the headlines. He describes severe shortages of food, medicine and clean water, alongside disease outbreaks and collapsing sanitation. The discussion also explores Israeli public opinion, Iran’s military pressure on Israel, and what Ponton sees as the failure of Western governments and mainstream media to confront or adequately report the scale of the crisis. PLEASE NOTE: These are complex and sensitive issues, and we aim to provide a balanced conversation. As always, we encourage you to listen, reflect, and explore the various perspectives, including Alon Roth Snir, Vanessa Beeley, Greg Simons and RCR hosts Simon O’Connor and Rodney Hide. Discover more from 21st Century Wire or find them on X Follow Freddie on X

youtube.title: KYLIE CRONWRIGHT
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Kylie Cronwright, a food preservation educator and founder of Patch to Pantry, about the growing return to home cooking and self-sufficiency. Kylie explains how her background in food technology and experiences during COVID-19 and Cyclone Gabrielle fuelled interest in preserving and pantry building. They explore simple entry points like chutneys, dehydrating, and bulk storage, while challenging reliance on processed food. They highlight how even small households can build resilience, save money, and reconnect with traditional skills through practical, everyday food preparation. For further information: Check out the Masterclass replay: Start preserving food at home visit the Patch to Pantry and Kiwi Family Kitchen websites

youtube.title: JASON TEH
youtube.summary: Jason Teh, Senior Analyst and Portfolio Manager at Clime Investment Management, joins Paul Brennan to discuss Australia’s fuel vulnerability with reserves sitting at roughly 30 days, far below the 90-day international benchmark.. The shift away from domestic refining toward cheaper Asian imports has eroded resilience, while governments are now scrambling to secure supply and storage. Jason highlights the need for long-term energy security planning, including diversified sources and stronger reserves to withstand future disruptions. For more information visit the Clime website

youtube.title: GREENWASHED
youtube.summary: Jaspreet Boparai and Don Nicolson unpack the climate scenario RCP8.5, once widely used in modelling and now under growing scrutiny. They explore how it has shaped coastal risk maps, LIM reports, and property values, and why homeowners may want to ask what assumptions sit behind the numbers. For further information: Local Government Official Information and Meetings Amendment Act 2023 Southland District Council: Coastal Hazards In the case of the Southland Coast and Rakiura Stewart Island, Sea Level Rise & Extreme Sea Level Exposure Spatial Forecasting Technical Report, 765 properties in Southland are affected in some of the scenarios. Ministry for the Environment: Aotearoa New Zealand climate change projections More information on deciding which emissions scenario to use can be found in Aotearoa New Zealand’s first national adaptation plan which recommends the middle-of-the-road emissions scenario (SSP2-4.5, RCP4.5) and the fossil fuel-intensive development scenario (SSP5-8.5, RCP8.5) be used for detailed hazard and risk assessments in both coastal and non-coastal areas. It is appropriate to consider more than one scenario for stress testing due to the complexity of being a project

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms joins Paul Brennan to talk about random violence in Melbourne, and broad concern about crime and public safety. They discuss cultural tensions at sporting events, debates over gender-neutral facilities and scepticism around government vaccination campaigns. They also cover key political developments, fuel security and ongoing economic pressures. Discover more from Tim at The Unshackled

youtube.title: CLARE SWINNEY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by citizen journalist Clare Swinney, to discuss her concerns over bird flu planning in New Zealand, which she says echo Covid-era responses. A whistleblower from a North Island council in contact with Swinney says agencies are quietly expanding contingency plans, including surveillance, PPE stockpiles, and potential mass culling, with limited public scrutiny.

youtube.title: SUZANNE LEVY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with Suzanne Levy of Speak Up for Women, about a nationwide review of council swimming pool facilities, which found most are labelled single-sex but often operate as mixed-sex due to unclear or gender-identity policies. Only a small number of councils were identified as maintaining clearly female-only spaces, while many lacked firm guidelines altogether. For more information check out the Speak Up For Women website

youtube.title: TECH TUESDAY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Steven Sykes explore how AI is reshaping cybersecurity, as long-hidden vulnerabilities in code are uncovered. They also discuss increasing data collection in everyday technology and discuss how constant updates, surveillance and subscriptions are quietly redefining ownership and control in modern digital life.

youtube.title: THE BRENNAN BAROMETER
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan delivers an impromptu “Brennan Barometer” reacting to a tense exchange in Nelson, where Sue Grey of the NZ Outdoors and Freedom Party questioned Chris Hipkins about vaccine-related harm. Paul reinforces his message from earlier Barometers: slowly, slowly catchy monkey.

Does the party's own position on political donations still stack up? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/peter-williams-on-politics-dont-dismiss-top-a-genuine-threat-to-the-centre-right #RCRMedia

youtube.title: FREDDIE PONTON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is rejoined by Freddie Ponton, Associate Editor at 21st Century Wire. This week they discuss escalating tensions in the Gulf and the breakdown of meaningful negotiations between the United States and Iran. Ongoing military actions, deep mistrust, and competing agendas leave the situation in stalemate. Ponton says shifting alliances and strained Western credibility are accelerating a broader geopolitical realignment. Discover more from 21st Century Wire or find them on X Follow Freddie on X

youtube.title: PAUL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan mailbag touches on fuel security, global conflict, health debates and media trust. There is praise for guests like Alia Bland, Katie Ashby-Koppens, Steven Sykes, and Art Berman, alongside scepticism about war coverage and claims of fear-driven narratives. Listeners also share personal experiences, practical resilience ideas and strong political views, revealing a deeply engaged audience grappling with uncertainty, preparedness and competing interpretations of global events.
